proof:
The first-order affine margin increment is $\alpha\cdot(z-p)+v\cdot(x-y)+\delta\,v\cdot\Sigma u/G(u)$; on the old plane this is $D\cdot\xi$. The actual perturbed margin differs from this affine-in-time approximation by $O(t^2)$ uniformly. For small $t$ the continuous coefficient has norm bounded below by $\|u\|/2$. The disagreement of the captures lies in a strip of width $O(t^2)$ in each bounded fiber and changes volume by $O(t^2)$ by Fubini. Thus the derivative is unchanged by the remainder. The first two slicing paragraphs in the proof of b319e7dcda1486e9 apply to each fixed positive convex fiber with this affine perturbation, after dividing the old and increment margins by $\|u\|$. In these paragraphs only the local interval calculation is used. It applies to any starting nonvertical plane and any affine increment. On lines crossing the interior of a proper section the derivative is the full margin increment. On inside and outside support the interval clips it to its negative and positive parts, respectively. Null tangential sections contribute zero, including the single-point counting convention at $d=1$. These give the displayed derivative. The identity $\delta u^{\mathsf T}\Sigma u/G(u)=\delta G(u)$ gives $(a,u)\cdot\xi=0$; subtracting a radial variation can therefore enforce tangency to $G(u)=1$ without changing the derivative in that chart.

The moment sets are compact convex by weak-* compactness of the densities bounded between zero and one, with Borel representatives and continuous finite-dimensional moments. Their support functions are the positive-part integrals by pointwise choice of the indicator of the positive margin. The derivative is the support function of $m+Z(\theta_O)$ minus that of $-Z(\theta_I)$. Comparing the support functions in every direction gives the inclusion and its density quantifiers. Expanding positive parts and taking the two directions $D,-D$ gives the centered inequality. At any local minimum all these derivatives are nonnegative. If $\theta_O=0$, the inequality forces $\int|D\cdot\xi|d\theta_I=0$ for every $D$. Test a basis to get $\xi=0$ almost everywhere on inside support. Non-own fibers have $z-p\ne0$, and the proper own trace contributes no inside support. Hence $\theta_I=0$. The inclusion then gives $m=0$; the proper own section has positive coarea, so division by the total proper coarea gives the stated centroid.

statement:
Let $\mu$ sum $d$-volumes on finitely many positive-volume compact convex fibers, $d\ge1$. Fix $Y=(p,y)$, $\delta>0$, and positive definite $\Sigma$. For $u\ne0$, put $G(u)=(u^{\mathsf T}\Sigma u)^{1/2}$, and let $H(a,u)$ have margin $a\cdot(z-p)+u\cdot(x-y)+\delta G(u)$. Use the nonnegative side as the cap. On its old plane set $\xi=(z-p,x-y+\delta\Sigma u/G(u))$. Let $\theta_P,\theta_I,\theta_O$ be the sums of section $\mathcal H^{d-1}/\|u\|$ over proper, inside-supporting (full capture), and outside-supporting (zero capture) traces, with $\mathcal H^0$ counting. For a normal increment $D=(\alpha,v)$ the raw right derivative is
$
\int D\cdot\xi\,d\theta_P-\int(-D\cdot\xi)_+\,d\theta_I+\int(D\cdot\xi)_+\,d\theta_O.
$
Strictly saturated fibers contribute zero, and $(a,u)\cdot\xi=0$ on the old plane.

Put $m=\int \xi\,d\theta_P$ and $Z(\theta)=\{\int q\xi\,d\theta: q\text{ Borel},\ 0\le q\le1\}$. The derivative is nonnegative for every $D$ exactly when $-Z(\theta_I)\subseteq m+Z(\theta_O)$, or equivalently when every inside density $q_I$ admits an outside density $q_O$ with $m+\int q_I\xi\,d\theta_I+\int q_O\xi\,d\theta_O=0$. Equivalently for every $D$ one has
$
\left|D\cdot m+\tfrac12\int D\cdot\xi\,d(\theta_I+\theta_O)\right|
\le \tfrac12\left(\int|D\cdot\xi|\,d\theta_O-\int|D\cdot\xi|\,d\theta_I\right).
$
If the own trace is proper, this condition with $\theta_O=0$ implies $\theta_I=0$ and that the coarea-weighted proper-section centroid is $(p,y-\delta\Sigma u/G(u))$. In particular a positive-area inside supporting trace at a normal local minimum requires a positive-area outside supporting trace.
